evals.prompt: I just finished adding a dark mode toggle to my Next.js app. The component is in src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx and it uses next-themes. I've tested it manually and it works. /go
evals.expected_output: Detects web-app project type, starts dev server, verifies the page loads (ideally navigates to the theme toggle), runs /simplify on changed files, creates a PR with testing evidence
expectations: Detects the project as a web-app or fullstack type
Attempts to start the dev server
Runs the existing test suite if one exists
Invokes the /simplify skill or equivalent code review
Creates a PR or invokes ce-commit-push-pr
Reports a summary with testing, simplify, and PR status

evals.prompt: ok so I added a new POST /api/webhooks/stripe endpoint to handle subscription changes. It validates the webhook signature, updates the user's plan in the database, and sends a confirmation email. The code is in src/routes/webhooks.ts. /go
evals.expected_output: Detects backend-api project type, starts the server, tests the webhook endpoint with curl, runs /simplify, creates PR
expectations: Detects the project as a backend-api type
Attempts to start the backend server
Tests the API endpoint with curl or similar
Creates a PR with details about what was tested

evals.prompt: I just built a Chrome extension that highlights all prices on any webpage and converts them to EUR using a live exchange rate. The manifest.json is set up, content script injects into all pages, and the popup lets you pick your target currency. /go
evals.expected_output: Detects chrome-extension project type, builds the extension, verifies build output, optionally loads in browser, runs /simplify, creates PR
expectations: Detects the project as a chrome-extension type via manifest.json inspection
Runs the build command if one exists
Verifies the built extension has valid structure
Reports a summary with testing, simplify, and PR status
